source_text.body:
Pull nutrition and fitness data into one dashboard
A poster set up a tracker via Claude in Chrome that gathers Cronometer and Fitbit or Google Health data in one place.
·
Jun 23, 2026
Done with
CH
Claude in Chrome
What they did
The poster set up a Claude project in Chrome that built a tracker/dashboard pulling data from Cronometer and Fitbit or Google Health. After feeding Claude their health goals, they had it run as a 7 a.m. scheduled task: fetch the latest nutrition, sleep, recovery, and workout data, analyze the previous day and weekly averages, then send a morning briefing with updated step and protein goals, meal suggestions, and that day’s workout.
How it went
It worked well enough that they said they look forward to the briefing every morning, and it adapted plans using recovery, cycle phase, and upcoming restaurant plans. It fell short in one place: they wanted it as a phone app but couldn’t figure that out, so it stayed a dashboard/project.
Worth knowing
The main catch was setup by iteration: they said they did not design all the logic upfront and instead kept tweaking the system inside Claude as they noticed things.
Try it yourself
with
Claude in Chrome
Copy prompt
Using my logged-in browser, open [Cronometer] and [Fitbit or Google Health] and pull my [calories, macros, steps, sleep, weight] for the last [number] days. Put them in one table or simple dashboard in [Google Sheet or local HTML file], one row per day. Don't change any settings or data on those sites, and stop when the combined view is ready and you have told me any days with missing data.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/ClaudeHomies/comments/1u757n0/so_what_did_you_do_with_claude_today_not_coding
